hints: Find the peak of the intensity curve and read its wavelength from the horizontal axis in $\text{nm}$ - it is near $100$ to $200\text{ nm}$.
Recall the order of the spectrum by wavelength: X-ray shortest, then ultraviolet, then visible light at about $400$ to $700\text{ nm}$, then infrared longest.
Check which named band contains about $140\text{ nm}$ and has much higher intensity than the $400$-$1000\text{ nm}$ tail.
walkthrough: Read the wavelength of maximum intensity from the graph. The highest point of the curve is at about $140\text{ nm}$ on the wavelength axis.

Recall the approximate EM bands: X-ray below about $10\text{ nm}$, ultraviolet from about $10\text{ nm}$ to $400\text{ nm}$, visible light from about $400\text{ nm}$ to $700\text{ nm}$, and infrared above about $700\text{ nm}$.
Compare the peak value of about $140\text{ nm}$ with these limits. It is shorter than visible light but much longer than X-rays.
Therefore the maximum lies in the ultraviolet region. This is option C

options.A: Infrared is wavelengths longer than about $700\text{ nm}$, where the graph shows intensity close to zero, not the peak.
options.B: Visible light is about $400$ to $700\text{ nm}$, which is on the low tail of the curve, well past the maximum.
options.C: The peak is at about $140\text{ nm}$, which lies between X-rays and visible light in the ultraviolet range of about $10$ to $400\text{ nm}$.
options.D: X-rays have wavelengths below about $10\text{ nm}$, where the graph shows almost zero intensity before the curve rises.
